note: Libraries, archives, temples, schools and guild halls of Aethwyrd and the draft books on their shelves (12_Systems/libraries_and_books.md). Books are drafts, not Canon, until the user approves them. A library with status 'proposed' is not Canon either.

libraries.name: Brindlewick Guild Branch Shelf
libraries.source: Data/World/gazetteer.json (Whisperwood: the guild branch); 10_World/brindlewick.md (Magistra Eolande Fairweather, mage trainer and librarian)
libraries.blurb: The guild branch where most adventurers wake up keeps a small shelf for newcomers, tended by the village's mage trainer.

libraries.name: Aldmere Royal and Noble Archives
libraries.source: 10_World/world.md (Aldmere City, five districts); 02_Lore/history.md (royal and noble archives)
libraries.blurb: Copies of reeve's papers, valley records and travellers' notes kept in the crown city, with the road to the Labyrinth entrance below it.

libraries.name: The Mages' Academy Library
libraries.source: 02_Lore/history.md (Mages' Academy, est. 512); 10_World/world.md (Aldmere City Academy district)
libraries.blurb: Lectures, copied demonstrations and the careful fragments of the old empire, kept where magic is taught.

libraries.name: Aldmere Guild Hall Reading Room
libraries.source: The Guild exists in Canon (Section 2 ranks); a reading room in its Aldmere hall is proposed
libraries.blurb: Branch manuals, street-law notes and the guild's copies of local rules.

libraries.name: Summoning Cathedral Shelf
libraries.source: 10_World/world.md (Aldmere City: Summoning Cathedral, Temple district)
libraries.blurb: Myth tellings and chapel notes left by pilgrims and keepers, shelved by the shrine floor.

libraries.name: The Peat Library
libraries.source: Data/World/gazetteer.json (Greymoor landmark: The Peat Library, a cave where the bog preserved a monastery's books)
libraries.blurb: A bog-cave where a drowned monastery's books are dried and read with care.

libraries.name: Lothaniel Root Archive
libraries.source: Proposed reading room in Sylvaran's canopy city (settlement in gazetteer)
libraries.blurb: Living-timber shelves kept by the canopy city, covering the mossy and summer lands around it.

libraries.name: Lirian Licence Archive
libraries.source: Proposed; Lirian's lock-licence quarrels (gazetteer) suggest a records house
libraries.blurb: The canal cities keep every lock licence and, beside them, the grain and market notes of the trunk river.

libraries.name: Vharlen Legion Records House
libraries.source: Proposed; Vharlen's frontier legions (gazetteer) would keep muster and road records
libraries.blurb: Muster books, route notes and soldiers' letters from the northern frontier.

libraries.name: Bastion Watch Library
libraries.source: Proposed; Bastion's outer ring (gazetteer) is a defensive town
libraries.blurb: A watch-house shelf of field notes about the dark country the Bastion stands against.

libraries.name: Karak Dûn Hall of Records
libraries.source: Proposed; Karak Dûn is canon (gazetteer); oath and craft records are implied by the Oath-Anvil tradition
libraries.blurb: Craft marks, oath records and the working notes of the mines and the clockwork halls.

libraries.name: Shen-Lu Foothill Sect Library
libraries.source: Proposed; Shen-Lu sect foothill towns (gazetteer)
libraries.blurb: A sect library of rules, practice notes and gate-town letters, open to guests who ask politely.

libraries.name: Hoshizora Shrine Library
libraries.source: Proposed; household shrines of Hoshizora (gazetteer)
libraries.blurb: River-mouth shrine shelves of festival notes, rain tables and household books.

libraries.name: Fox Shrine Isle Library
libraries.source: Data/World/gazetteer.json (Kitsune Isles: Fox Shrine, The Ninefold Shrine)
libraries.blurb: Stair-top shrine shelves where stories arrive by boat and leave changed.

libraries.name: Dragon-Bone Monastery Library
libraries.source: Data/World/gazetteer.json (Dragon Spine: the Bone Road links every monastery)
libraries.blurb: Monastery shelves along the Bone Road, with copies sent up to the eyries.

libraries.name: Skjaldheim Skald Hall
libraries.source: Proposed; Skjaldheim is canon (gazetteer); a skald hall is implied by longhouse culture
libraries.blurb: Sagas, weather notes and ice-country road books kept in the fjord-head hall.

libraries.name: Qadira Water Archive
libraries.source: Proposed in 02_Lore/history.md (Sunscar: build a water archive, draft)
libraries.blurb: Water-keepers' recitations and well records of the desert oasis and the dune country around it.

libraries.name: Zaruma Earth Towers
libraries.source: 02_Lore/history.md (Zaruma: a kingdom of scholars; library-mosque-style towers of earth)
libraries.blurb: Griots and scribes keep the kingdom's histories in earth towers along the gold road.

libraries.name: Port Goldmere Harbor Reading Room
libraries.source: Proposed; Port Goldmere is canon (gazetteer)
libraries.blurb: Tide tables, trade notes and sailors' songs kept by the harbor masters.

libraries.name: Xochitl Cord Archive
libraries.source: Proposed in 02_Lore/history.md (treat the cords as a land and labor archive, draft)
libraries.blurb: Knotted records and river-city ledgers, read aloud by those who keep the cords.

libraries.name: Lumbaya Sky Temple Shelf
libraries.source: Data/World/gazetteer.json (Lumbaya: The Sky Temple)
libraries.blurb: Temple village shelves of chapel notes, pilgrim letters and valley histories.

libraries.name: Zarvan Garden Library
libraries.source: Proposed; Zarvan's garden cities are canon (gazetteer)
libraries.blurb: Terrace-garden reading rooms of aqueduct, planting and cliff-town notes.

libraries.name: Aurumdeep Explorers' Camp Shelf
libraries.source: Data/World/gazetteer.json (Aurumdeep explorers' camp; Labyrinth back-door from floor 30)
libraries.blurb: Explorers leave their notes here for the next party: deep-country field notes and letters.

libraries.name: The Upside-Down Library (Floor 72)
libraries.source: Data/World/gazetteer.json (a scholar wants a book from the upside-down library on floor seventy-two, read in the right direction)
libraries.blurb: A library hanging the wrong way up, whose books must be read in the right direction.
